correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact decomposition R(n)=P(gcd(n,X)>1)-E_n for X~Bin(n,1/2). Every reduced coefficient is no larger than the original coefficient by a block-union injection; 0<=E_n<=(n+1)2^{-n/2} since n/g<=n/2 on the nonprimitive indices. For every divisor d, centered indicator 1_{d|k}-1/d has partial sums in [0,1]. Abel summation against unimodal binomial probabilities bounds |P(d|X)-1/d| by 2M_n, *uniformly in d*, including d>sqrt(n). Mobius inversion over all d|n gives 2 tau(n) M_n. The divisor convolution bound sum_{n<=N}tau(n)/sqrt(n)=O(sqrt(N)(1+log N)), combined with the classical exact summatory totient ratio 6N/pi^2+O(log N), proves the mean rate. Prime and primorial limits follow using P(gcd(p,k)>1) endpoint behavior and the diverging sum of reciprocal primes. Independently enumerated 500 exact integer binomial rows and checked every pointwise bound. No finite test is used to infer the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The original OEIS sequence A271834 explicitly asks whether the mean normalized binomial-row deficit converges and records only an approximation near 0.3915. The exact 1-6/pi^2 answer and quantitative uniform pointwise totient profile resolve this naturally posed arithmetic problem and explain oscillations with liminf zero and limsup one. This is more than elementary restatement of a known formula: it settles the previously stated infinite mean and links it to a standard multiplicative invariant.

final_claim: For every integer n>=1, R(n) differs from 1-phi(n)/n by at most 2 tau(n)2^{-n} C(n,floor(n/2))+(n+1)2^{-n/2}; its Cesaro mean is 1-6/pi^2 with O((1+log N)/sqrt(N)) error; R(p)=0 for primes while primorials approach one.
limitations: Absolute pointwise error need not be optimal; no convergence of R(n) itself, indeed liminf=0 and limsup=1. Source inspections do not certify absolute historical priority.
